tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

schema.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

## Roles and lifetimes in the request (approved 2026-10-29)

Decided by Kenneth in the side session "Chat history cache handoff" (`local_97f342dd-4367-4bc5-830d-1c6d6d91db47`), relayed to this doc; his words: "ok. go with your proposal." The provider-doc citations below are that session's, not re-verified here.

**Append-only record, separate from visibility.** Each chat keeps an append-only record of every item ever sent to the model. A request renders that record plus the new items. No item is rewritten, dropped or re-derived; what the model should still see is a lifetime flag per item, never an edit of the record. Source cited: Anthropic's mid-conversation system messages doc (`platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages`): a cleared message stays in the array but renders nothing, must be re-sent verbatim, and rebuilding or dropping it counts as an edit to an earlier message that fails the thinking check and breaks the cache.

**Three roles, assigned by who speaks, never by lifetime:**

| Role | Wire | Carries |
|---|---|---|
| Operator, standing | Anthropic top-level `system`; Responses `instructions` | Standing prompt and tools, written once per chat, never changed |
| Operator, in conversation | Anthropic in-array `role:"system"` (Opus 5.5 and 5.x, not Sonnet 5); OpenAI `developer` item | Situational instructions (skills; the file-load reminder if it survives D4) and app observations (notes: slice finished, hand setup change, calibration handover). The doc names "state changes your application observes" as a use case and distinguishes a user message (from the end user) from a system message (from the operator) |
| End user | `user` | The person's words plus what travels with them: workspace block, plate picture, file report. Kept in the record as sent (closes R4) |
| Tool results | `tool_result` / `function_call_output` | Their own channel, never promoted; the doc forbids relaying third-party content through system messages |

**Lifetimes.** Skills and the reminder clear at the next user message on Anthropic (`clear_at: "next_user_message"`, beta header `mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`). OpenAI has no clear, so they stay visible and should be kept short. Notes the model replied to stay visible on both providers. Thinking/reasoning is stored per chat and replayed.

**Behaviour changes, so evals are required.** Kenneth confirmed this changes what the model reads. Per his 2026-10-19 rule (last confirmed results are the baseline), every behaviour-changing step runs live prompt evals against a baseline. Baselines needed before any such step: OpenAI journeys (none exist) and the prompt-case set (check the last confirmed model and date). Request-body logging in the harness comes before all of it.

**Risks recorded, not resolved:**

- `clear_at` is a beta feature.
- Sonnet 5.5 / Haiku 5.5 may ignore a system message placed right after a tool result, so a note landing there needs a placement rule.
- OpenAI accumulates visible skill text (1.3–8.5 KB each); whether that changes answers is an eval question.
- Unverified whether the top-level `system` field and in-array system messages may coexist in one request (the doc implies yes).
- Unverified how the JusPrin Cloud gateway passes in-array system messages through in its Anthropic wire format. Production goes through the gateway, so check before R7.
- Corrections the side session made to its own earlier claims, so the tracker does not carry them: Anthropic does accept system messages inside `messages` on 5.x models; OpenAI's `instructions` parameter inserts a system/developer message rather than sitting above both.

## Phase 0: ground truth (done)

input.old_string: ## Phase 0: ground truth (done)
input.new_string:
## Roles and lifetimes in the request (approved 2026-10-29)

Decided by Kenneth in the side session "Chat history cache handoff" (`local_97f342dd-4367-4bc5-830d-1c6d6d91db47`), relayed to this doc; his words: "ok. go with your proposal." The provider-doc citations below are that session's, not re-verified here.

**Append-only record, separate from visibility.** Each chat keeps an append-only record of every item ever sent to the model. A request renders that record plus the new items. No item is rewritten, dropped or re-derived; what the model should still see is a lifetime flag per item, never an edit of the record. Source cited: Anthropic's mid-conversation system messages doc (`platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages`): a cleared message stays in the array but renders nothing, must be re-sent verbatim, and rebuilding or dropping it counts as an edit to an earlier message that fails the thinking check and breaks the cache.

**Three roles, assigned by who speaks, never by lifetime:**

| Role | Wire | Carries |
|---|---|---|
| Operator, standing | Anthropic top-level `system`; Responses `instructions` | Standing prompt and tools, written once per chat, never changed |
| Operator, in conversation | Anthropic in-array `role:"system"` (Opus 5.5 and 5.x, not Sonnet 5); OpenAI `developer` item | Situational instructions (skills; the file-load reminder if it survives D4) and app observations (notes: slice finished, hand setup change, calibration handover). The doc names "state changes your application observes" as a use case and distinguishes a user message (from the end user) from a system message (from the operator) |
| End user | `user` | The person's words plus what travels with them: workspace block, plate picture, file report. Kept in the record as sent (closes R4) |
| Tool results | `tool_result` / `function_call_output` | Their own channel, never promoted; the doc forbids relaying third-party content through system messages |

**Lifetimes.** Skills and the reminder clear at the next user message on Anthropic (`clear_at: "next_user_message"`, beta header `mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`). OpenAI has no clear, so they stay visible and should be kept short. Notes the model replied to stay visible on both providers. Thinking/reasoning is stored per chat and replayed.

**Behaviour changes, so evals are required.** Kenneth confirmed this changes what the model reads. Per his 2026-10-19 rule (last confirmed results are the baseline), every behaviour-changing step runs live prompt evals against a baseline. Baselines needed before any such step: OpenAI journeys (none exist) and the prompt-case set (check the last confirmed model and date). Request-body logging in the harness comes before all of it.

**Risks recorded, not resolved:**

- `clear_at` is a beta feature.
- Sonnet 5.5 / Haiku 5.5 may ignore a system message placed right after a tool result, so a note landing there needs a placement rule.
- OpenAI accumulates visible skill text (1.3–8.5 KB each); whether that changes answers is an eval question.
- Unverified whether the top-level `system` field and in-array system messages may coexist in one request (the doc implies yes).
- Unverified how the JusPrin Cloud gateway passes in-array system messages through in its Anthropic wire format. Production goes through the gateway, so check before R7.
- Corrections the side session made to its own earlier claims, so the tracker does not carry them: Anthropic does accept system messages inside `messages` on 5.x models; OpenAI's `instructions` parameter inserts a system/developer message rather than sitting above both.

## Phase 0: ground truth (done)

The side session "Chat history cache handoff" ([local_97f342dd](#local_97f342dd-4367-4bc5-830d-1c6d6d91db47)) reported that you approved its roles-and-lifetimes design for the Agent chat request. I have folded that into [chat-history-cache-plan.md](chat-history-cache-plan.md). The doc stays untracked; nothing is committed or pushed.

What changed in the tracker:

- **D1 decided.** Each chat keeps an append-only record of every item ever sent, thinking included, pictures as blob references. What the model still sees is a lifetime flag per item, never an edit of the record.
- **D2 decided.** App notes become operator-role in-conversation messages: Anthropic in-array `system`, OpenAI `developer`. Kept in the record, never cleared, same treatment in project and printer chat. This replaces the "JusPrin app note, not the person's words" prefix in user text.
- **D4 narrowed.** The file-load reminder is either deleted or becomes a turn-scoped operator message like a skill. You have not picked between the two.
- **New section "Roles and lifetimes"** holds the three-role table, the clear-at rule (Anthropic clears skills at the next user message, OpenAI cannot clear so they stay short), and the six open risks. The two that gate R7 are whether the top-level system field and in-array system messages may coexist, and how the JusPrin Cloud gateway passes in-array system messages through. I recorded the side session's provider-doc citations as its claims, not as re-verified here.
- **R steps reworded.** R2 and R6 now name the operator role. R8 gains "always offer `object_import`" so the tool list never changes. A prerequisite line says every model-visible step needs harness request-body logging first, then baselines: OpenAI journeys, which do not exist yet, and the prompt-case set on its last confirmed model.

Still open and yours: D3 (real context limit), the D4 pick, the D5 commit pointer, D6 spend, D7 TTL, D8 `prompt_cache_key`. The request-body logging is the one piece of work with nothing in front of it.

| R3 Remove the 64 KiB rolling trim and the 16 KiB result cut; put the real limit in their place | D3 | not started |
| R4 Keep earlier messages' workspace blocks in the record (user role, as sent) | guard | not started |
| R5 Keep pictures in the record (blob references; ~1,050 Anthropic tokens each) | guard | not started |
| R6 Project-chat notes move from user-text prefix to the operator role (Anthropic in-array `system`, OpenAI `developer`); printer chat's developer notes unchanged in role; kept in the record, never cleared | D2 decided; evals (model-visible); gateway pass-through check | not started |

input.prompt:
Add request-body logging to the shell harness so that every model request the Agent posts during a harness run is written to disk exactly as posted, one file per request, with the response's usage line beside it.

Where things are:
- The transport interface is `IAgentHttpTransport` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentTransport.hpp` (`post(AgentHttpRequest, EventFn)`); the Agent posts through it. The cleanest design is a logging transport in the harness that wraps whichever real or fake transport the harness builds, writes the body bytes before forwarding, and writes the usage/stop fields from the streamed response events after.
- The shell harness is `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp`; `--live-agent` is handled around line 13150. Find how the live and fake transports are built and wrap them there.
- The project-prompt recorder (`tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`, `requests.json`, its README) stores scripted bodies and cut stored results at 4,000 characters. Leave its format unchanged; the new log is a separate, uncut, byte-exact record.
- The Catch2 agent tests in `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp` show fake transports and streamed replies (`RecordingProvider`, `anthropic_stream`, `responses_stream`) you can reuse as models.

Deliverables:
1. A harness flag (for example `--request-log DIR`) that, when set, writes for each request `<n>-request.json` (bytes exactly as posted, plus a small sidecar or header with provider, endpoint, chat id and timestamp) and `<n>-response.json` (the usage and stop fields, and the final assembled response text if cheap to get). Numbering is per run, in post order. Works for both wire formats.
2. A Catch2 or harness test that drives a scripted (fake) run with the flag set and proves the file bytes equal what the transport posted, and that two requests give two files.
3. A small script `tests/project_prompt/prefix_check.py` that takes a log directory and, for consecutive requests of the same chat, reports the length of the common byte prefix, the first differing byte offset and the JSON path at which they diverge. This is the check phase 2 will use to find cache leaks. Give it a unit test on two tiny hand-written bodies.
4. A short section in `tests/shell/README.md` (or the harness's existing doc; find which one documents flags) on the flag and the script.

Done means: the agent suite and your new tests pass in your worktree's build; a scripted harness run with the flag produces files; nothing in `requests.json` or existing baselines changed; one or a few commits on your branch with messages that explain what and why; an untracked note `request-log-report.md` in the worktree root saying what you built, how you verified it, and anything you could not verify (there is no live run, say so).

1. `prompt_cache_key` on OpenAI Responses requests (`ResponsesCodec.cpp`). Yes, the production code should be simpler when this is done, with one part that grows on purpose. And the work is already delegated: the three sessions I started in the previous turn run on Opus 5.5, in their own worktrees, and I only review and merge what they produce.

**Why it gets simpler.** Today the history builder in `AgentHost.cpp` re-derives every earlier turn on each request: it retells assistant replies as text without thinking, cuts replayed results at 16 KiB, trims the whole history at 64 KiB, prepends the file-load reminder when no skill fired, prefixes notes as user text, strips workspace blocks and pictures, and drops skills. All of that is logic that exists only to make the history shorter or different from what was sent. Under D1 the chat keeps an append-only record of what was sent, and a request is "render the record plus the new items". Each of those mechanisms is deleted rather than replaced. The prototype's carry mechanism goes too.

**Where it grows, and why that is acceptable:**

- The operator role. Skills and notes become in-array `system` messages on Anthropic and `developer` items on OpenAI. That is a small role mapping in each codec where today's code is a string prefix in user text. A few lines each.
- R8. A `prompt_cache_key` field and an error path for `object_import` called with nothing to import. Both are a handful of lines.
- R3b, the visible compaction at the real context limit. This is the one real addition. D3 chose a compaction the person can see over a silent trim, so about twenty lines of trim become a chat item plus the lifetime-flag change on earlier items. It is new behaviour, not a bigger version of the old one.

Test code grows and should: the guard test, the harness logging and the prefix-check script are how we stop guessing. I don't count them.

**How you can hold me to it.** I added a rule to the plan doc: every merge onto `claude/chat-history-cache` records the production diff stat separately from tests, and any step with net new production lines must say why in its commit message. The table starts with R0 so the baseline is visible. If a merge comes back larger than the list above, that is a sign the session reimplemented something instead of deleting it, and I will send it back rather than merge it.

# R8 report: cache hygiene in the Agent's request building

Working doc, 2026-10-29, session `cache-r8`. Untracked: never commit it.
Branch `claude/cache-r8-f275c7`, cut from `claude/chat-history-cache` at `cd4162fa97`. Nothing pushed or merged.

## Summary

OpenAI requests now carry a `prompt_cache_key` naming the chat, except through the JusPrin Cloud gateway, which would refuse it with a 400. `object_import` is now offered on every request, so a chat's tool list never changes and an attachment no longer voids the Anthropic cache. The Anthropic breakpoint was left where it is: under R2 it is exactly where Anthropic's docs require it, and moving it onto the skill would be a 400 error there.

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `a08d17471f` | Item 1: per-chat `prompt_cache_key` on OpenAI Responses requests |
| `23cfa48bd1` | Item 2: `object_import` offered always; a call with nothing to import fails with `invalid_arguments` |
| `c5bd57c8eb` | Item 1 follow-up: the shell harness's prompt recorder leaves the per-run key out of `requests.json` |

Tests:

- **Agent suite** (`agent_bridge_tests`, default run):
  - before: 470 cases, 16,425 assertions, all passing
  - after: 473 cases, 16,490 assertions, all passing
- **`[history-prefix]` guard:**

  - after: identical, with the same first differences
  - The saved output is in `r8-guard-before.txt`.

## 1. `prompt_cache_key` (decision D8)

**What changed.**

- **Where the key comes from.** `AgentRequest` gained `chat_key`. `AgentHost::make_agent_request` sets it to `<projectId>/<conversationId>`, for example `p-3f…9a-1c…77/c-2`. That is one added line in `AgentHost.cpp`, next to `request_id`.
- **How it reaches the codec.** `ProviderAgent::begin_transcript` copies it to `TurnTranscript::chat_key`.
- **What the codec sends.** `ResponsesCodec::build` sends it as `prompt_cache_key` on reply requests.

**Why a new field was needed.** The chat id was not available at the codec before. `request_id` contains the project and chat ids, but also the message id and attempt, so it changes on every turn.

**When no key is sent:**

- **Title requests.** They have no `chat_key`.
- **The account provider (JusPrin Cloud, `account_sign_in`).** See the gateway section.
- **Length.** A project id is at most 35 characters (`"p-"` plus two 64-bit hex numbers, `default_uuid()` in `ProjectPersistence.cpp`), so keys are about 40 characters. OpenAI's limit is undocumented. One community report says 64 characters; **unverified**.

**Tests.**

- `test_agent_bridge.cpp`, "every request of a chat carries one prompt_cache_key, and another chat another". It runs on the real host and loop. Chat A has a person turn with a slice call (two requests) and the app's turn after the slice. Chat B has one request. All three of chat A's requests carry `projectId/c-1`, and chat B's carries `projectId/c-2`.
- `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp`, "a request carries its chat's prompt_cache_key, except through JusPrin's gateway and for a title". It is a codec-level test covering:
  - OpenAI and OpenRouter get the key
  - the gateway does not
  - a title request does not
  - an empty key sends nothing

The `[history-prefix]` guard compares every non-prompt body field across requests. It stays unchanged, which confirms that the key does not vary within a chat.

**OpenRouter.** Its Responses API reference lists `prompt_cache_key` as an accepted optional string, but does not say what it does. Whether OpenRouter forwards it to OpenAI is **unverified**.

### Gateway finding (verified by reading the source)

The gateway source is on this machine: `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise`, branch `master` at `7ab63cc151`, the same as `origin/master`. See `web_ent/jusprin/v2/upstream.py`.

- **Unknown fields are refused, not forwarded.** `ALLOWED_FIELDS['responses']` is `model, store, stream, parallel_tool_calls, instructions, tools, input, reasoning`. `prepare()` answers any other top-level field with `400 invalid_request "Field "prompt_cache_key" is not allowed."`. Sending the key through the gateway would have failed every OpenAI-format JusPrin Cloud request. That is why the codec skips it for `account_sign_in`.
- **The gateway is where the key matters most.** Every JusPrin Cloud user shares one OpenAI organisation, and the gateway prepends the same identity line to `instructions`. So all cloud chats open identically and land on the same cache machines.
  - **Follow-up:** add `prompt_cache_key` to `ALLOWED_FIELDS['responses']` in tsd-enterprise and deploy it. Then drop `&& !profile.account_sign_in` in `ResponsesCodec::build`.
  - **Order matters:** the app change must not ship before the gateway one.
  - Whether the deployed gateway matches `master` is **unverified**. The plan says it went live 2026-10-25 as obi.4048.
- **Anthropic format.** `messages` are forwarded as sent, `cache_control` included, and the gateway's identity text goes in a block of its own before the client's `system` block. Only `metadata` is dropped.
- **For R2/R6.**
  - In-array `role: "system"` messages and `developer` items pass through untouched, because the gateway does not inspect `messages` or `input`.
  - The gateway sends upstream only its backend's configured headers (`_headers()` in `upstream.py`), never the client's.
  - So R2's `clear_at` beta header (`anthropic-beta: mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`) reaches Anthropic only if it is added to the alias backend's `headers` in `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES`. Without it, `clear_at` is rejected as an unknown field.

## 2. A stable tool list

**Before.**

- `offered_tools` in `ProviderAgent.cpp` offered `object_import` only when the request's message had an importable model attachment. The turn that attached a model therefore sent a different tool list from the turn before and the turn after. On Anthropic that means a cold cache for the whole chat, twice.
- A call to `object_import` on any other turn was refused as `unknown_tool` before it ran.
- A call whose attachment could not be resolved failed with `not_found`: "The attached model is no longer available".

**Now.**

- **Registry.** `object_import` has `ToolAvailability::Always`. `ImportableAttachment` is removed from the enum.
- **Execution.** In `ToolExecutionCoordinator::execute`, an `attachmentId` that resolves to no stored model file fails with `invalid_arguments`, with the message: `No model file attached in this chat has the id "<id>". Nothing was imported. Use an attachment id from the person's message; if they attached no model file, ask them to attach it.`
- **Why `invalid_arguments`.**
  - It keeps the call in the "fix the call" group of `ToolErrors.hpp`, where `unknown_tool` already put it.
  - `not_found` means "read the state again, then call again", and re-reading the workspace cannot find an attachment.
  - The "Ask the person" codes (`opened_before`, `workspace_unavailable`) mean other conditions.
  - The message names the step.
- **Side effect.** A model attached in an earlier message of the chat can now be imported later, because the resolver looks the id up in the whole document.

**Tests.**

- `test_agent_bridge.cpp`, "the tool list is the same on every request of a chat, whatever a message attaches". It runs on the real host with the Anthropic wire format:
  - turn 1 has no attachment
  - turn 2 attaches a model and imports it, adding one object
  - turn 3 calls `object_import` with an id that names nothing
  - all 5 requests carry byte-identical `tools`, `object_import` included
  - the turn-3 call comes back as an `is_error` result with `invalid_arguments` and the message, and adds no object
- **Proved fail-first.** I temporarily put back the old rule (offer `object_import` only with an importable attachment), rebuilt and ran the test. It failed 5 of 28 assertions: the attachment turn's two requests carried a different tool list, and the turn-3 call got `unknown_tool`. I then restored the source.
- `test_tool_coordinator.cpp`: the unresolvable-attachment case now expects `invalid_arguments` and the exact message.
- `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp`: the tool list with a model attachment equals the list without one.
- Updated counts: from 29 to 30 tools in three tests.

**Knock-on changes outside the Agent sources.** Both are generated or test files, and both follow directly from the change:

- **`tests/project_prompt/project_tools.json`.**
  - Regenerated with `JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PROJECT_TOOLS=1`: 31 tools, 39,661 bytes compact, up from 38,792 (+869).
  - The README and a comment in `run_prompt_tests.py` were updated to match.
- **`tests/shell/project_prompt_scenario.inc`.**
  - The prompt recorder used to strip `object_import` before comparing a request's tools with `project_tools.json`. It now compares directly.
  - It also leaves `prompt_cache_key` out of recorded bodies; that is commit `c5bd57c8eb`.
  - The file compiles: the object file was built on its own.
  - The harness was **not run**, because that needs a full app build, which I did not start on the shared machine.
  - The shell-harness session (L0, `cache-log`) should know about this change.

**Behaviour change, not evaluated.** Every project-chat request now describes `object_import`, about 870 bytes, including turns with nothing attached. Per the plan's rule, steps that change what the model reads run the prompt evals. **No live evals were run.** That needs Kenneth's approval of a batch.

**Not changed.** `skill_read` is still offered only when the page lists skills. That list is fixed for a host session, and the printer sessions name their own tools, so it does not vary within a chat.

## 3. The Anthropic cache breakpoint and skill text

**Where the breakpoints are today** (`AnthropicCodec.cpp`, all `{"type":"ephemeral"}`):

1. The last tool (`tools_json`, line 87).
2. The single `system` block (`build`, line 272).
3. The last block of the newest `user` message after role normalisation (`build`, line 262). It moves forward on every request.

A fired skill is sent as an in-array `role: "system"` message right after the user content or the tool results that fired it (`push_skills`). Its picture is a user image block, which merges into that user message, so the picture sits before breakpoint 3 and is cached. The skill text sits after it.

- On the request that fires it, the skill text is billed uncached at 1x.
- On the next request of the turn it is written to the cache at 1.25x.

That is M1's leak.

**Bytes after the last breakpoint, 26 recorded bodies.**

- **Method.** Each body was mapped to the Anthropic codec's message layout: developer items become system messages, then the codec's merge and normalisation rules apply. Then I counted the compact JSON after the breakpoint block.
- **Script.** `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin--claude-worktrees-cache-r8-f275c7/c449884d-06ef-4be3-ae77-8382bf117ba4/scratchpad/r8/after_breakpoint.py`, run as `python3 -I <script> tests/project_prompt/requests.json`.
- **Scope.** The system prompt and tools, about 41 KB, come before breakpoints 1 and 2 and are not counted.

| case | after the last breakpoint today (bytes) | of which skill text |
|---|---|---|
| model-imported-by-tool, model-opened-by-tool, model-opened-unnamed | 8,520 each | 8,446 (file-loaded) |
| advice-infill, answer-from-context, direct-change, issue-explain, issue-fix, loaded-vs-configured, reply-in-german, slice-warnings-ready, troubleshoot-first-layer | 5,309 each | 5,210 (print issues) |
| slice-refused-by-tool, slice-refused-then-ready | 3,640 each | 3,577 (slice failed) |
| after-intent | 1,329 | 1,288 (setup changed) |
| the other 11 cases | 0 | 0 |

- 15 of 26 bodies have bytes after the breakpoint, totalling 81,950. In every case it is one trailing system message holding the skill.
- With a breakpoint on the skill it would be 0 in every case.

**Why I did not move the breakpoint.** Source: Anthropic's mid-conversation system messages page (`platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages`), read 2026-10-29.

- **Under R2 it is an error.** R2 sends skills as turn-scoped messages (`clear_at: "next_user_message"`). The page says such a message carries "no `cache_control`" ("A cleared message is never part of a cache key, so a breakpoint on it could never match"). The API answers `cache_control is not permitted on a turn-scoped system message` with a 400. It says to "Put the breakpoint on the last block of the preceding user turn instead". Its agent-loop example puts it on the last `tool_result`. That is exactly today's breakpoint 3.
- **Today it is undocumented.** For a plain (`clear_at: "never"`) system message, the page says it "is itself cacheable", and that on the next turn "you can move your cache breakpoint past it". It never says `cache_control` is allowed on its blocks. Verifying that would need a live call, so I made none.

The rule was to change the placement only if it is right under both today's behaviour and R2's. Moving the breakpoint onto the skill is right under neither for certain, and is a 400 under R2. The code is unchanged.

**Recommendation for R2.**

1. **Keep breakpoint 3 where it is**, on the last block of the newest user message, which is the user turn before any skill. Never put `cache_control` on a turn-scoped message.
2. **The leak goes away under R2 without a breakpoint change.** The page says a turn-scoped message "renders only while no `role: "user"` message comes after it" and "A user message that carries only `tool_result` blocks counts". A cleared message "costs no input tokens".
   - So under R2 a skill's text is billed once, on the request that fires it, and is never written to the cache.
   - Today the same text is billed at 1x, then written at 1.25x, then read on the turn's later requests.
   - The 81,950 bytes above stay after the breakpoint on the firing request, but stop being written to the cache one request late.
3. **The clearing request reads the right entry.** The page says that on the request that clears a message, "the reusable cached prefix ends at the user turn before it, so only the one assistant turn between that message and the new user message is reprocessed". The entry it reads is the one breakpoint 3 wrote on the firing request. That is another reason not to move breakpoint 3.
4. **A design point R2 must settle (behaviour, not cost).** Because a `tool_result` message clears a turn-scoped message, the model sees the skill only on the request that fired it, not "for the rest of the turn".
   - That matches what the Responses codec does today, since it drops the skill from the next request.
   - It does not match today's Anthropic codec, which keeps the skill visible for the rest of the turn.
   - If the plan's "cleared at the next user message" meant the next message from the person, `clear_at` does not do that.
5. **A message after a tool result on smaller models.** The plan already notes that Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 may ignore a system message placed right after a tool result. Under R2 that is the only place a skill fired by a result can go.

**TTL (decision D7).** Confirmed: the codec sends no `ttl`. `ephemeral()` is `{"type":"ephemeral"}` at all three breakpoints, so the 5-minute default applies. Nothing in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/` mentions `ttl` or `1h`. The gateway forwards `cache_control` unchanged.

# Request-body logging (L0): report

Untracked working note, 2026-10-29. Branch `claude/cache-request-log-eca52c`, commit `282342b918`, on top of `claude/chat-history-cache` (`cd4162fa97`). Not pushed or merged.

## Problem

The chat-history cache work has to check that each model request opens with the bytes of the one before it. No full request body was kept anywhere. The prompt-test recorder's `requests.json` holds bodies for its own suite, with stored results cut at 4,000 characters, and the live harness modes printed only token counts.

## What I built

- **`tests/jusprin_support/RequestLog.hpp`** (header-only, so the harness and `agent_bridge_tests` share it with no CMake change). `RequestLog::transport(provider, inner)` wraps any `IAgentHttpTransport`; `RequestLog::agent(inner)` wraps any `IAgentService`, so the log knows each request's purpose (reply or title), request id and attempt. For the n-th request of a run it writes:
  - `NNNN-request.json`: the body exactly as the transport was given it, written before it is forwarded.
  - `NNNN-request.meta.json`: provider, URL, headers (`Authorization`, `x-api-key` and other credential headers redacted; `Idempotency-Key` kept), project id and chat id (chat ids restart in each project), purpose, request id, attempt, post time, body length.
  - `NNNN-response.sse`: the response stream as received.
  - `NNNN-response.json`: outcome (complete, error, cancelled, replaced, not_started), HTTP status, usage with the provider's own field names (Anthropic `cache_read_input_tokens`/`cache_creation_input_tokens` come through as-is), stop reason, assembled text, error. It reads both the Messages and the Responses stream.
- **Shell harness flag `--request-log <dir>`**, for `--live-agent`, `--manual-live-agent` and `--project-prompt-requests`. It refuses a non-empty directory and any other mode (exit 2). Documented in the header comment of `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` (where all flags are documented; there is no `tests/shell/README.md`) and in a new section of `tests/project_prompt/README.md`.
- **`tests/project_prompt/prefix_check.py LOG_DIR [--ignore-key KEY] [--json]`**. For consecutive requests of the same project, chat and purpose it reports the common byte prefix, the first differing byte, the JSON path of that byte in each body, and the path of the last differing byte. `[append]` means the later body is the earlier one with items added at the end of one array and every other byte unchanged. `--ignore-key cache_control` drops Anthropic's moving breakpoint (then the bodies are compared as Python re-serialises them, and the output says so). Unit tests: `tests/project_prompt/test_prefix_check.py`.

## 1. `prompt_cache_key` (decision D8)

**What changed.**

- **Where the key comes from.** `AgentRequest` gained `chat_key`. `AgentHost::make_agent_request` sets it to `<projectId>/<conversationId>`, for example `p-3f…9a-1c…77/c-2`. That is one added line in `AgentHost.cpp`, next to `request_id`.
- **How it reaches the codec.** `ProviderAgent::begin_transcript` copies it to `TurnTranscript::chat_key`.
- **What the codec sends.** `ResponsesCodec::build` sends it as `prompt_cache_key` on reply requests.

**Why a new field was needed.** The chat id was not available at the codec before. `request_id` contains the project and chat ids, but also the message id and attempt, so it changes on every turn.

**When no key is sent:**

- **Title requests.** They have no `chat_key`.
- **The account provider (JusPrin Cloud, `account_sign_in`).** See the gateway section.
- **Length.** A project id is at most 35 characters (`"p-"` plus two 64-bit hex numbers, `default_uuid()` in `ProjectPersistence.cpp`), so keys are about 40 characters. OpenAI's limit is undocumented. One community report says 64 characters; **unverified**.

**Tests.**

- `test_agent_bridge.cpp`, "every request of a chat carries one prompt_cache_key, and another chat another". It runs on the real host and loop. Chat A has a person turn with a slice call (two requests) and the app's turn after the slice. Chat B has one request. All three of chat A's requests carry `projectId/c-1`, and chat B's carries `projectId/c-2`.
- `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp`, "a request carries its chat's prompt_cache_key, except through JusPrin's gateway and for a title". It is a codec-level test covering:
  - OpenAI and OpenRouter get the key
  - the gateway does not
  - a title request does not
  - an empty key sends nothing

The `[history-prefix]` guard compares every non-prompt body field across requests. It stays unchanged, which confirms that the key does not vary within a chat.

**OpenRouter.** Its Responses API reference lists `prompt_cache_key` as an accepted optional string, but does not say what it does. Whether OpenRouter forwards it to OpenAI is **unverified**.

### Gateway finding (verified by reading the source)

The gateway source is on this machine: `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise`, branch `master` at `7ab63cc151`, the same as `origin/master`. See `web_ent/jusprin/v2/upstream.py`.

- **Unknown fields are refused, not forwarded.** `ALLOWED_FIELDS['responses']` is `model, store, stream, parallel_tool_calls, instructions, tools, input, reasoning`. `prepare()` answers any other top-level field with `400 invalid_request "Field "prompt_cache_key" is not allowed."`. Sending the key through the gateway would have failed every OpenAI-format JusPrin Cloud request. That is why the codec skips it for `account_sign_in`.
- **The gateway is where the key matters most.** Every JusPrin Cloud user shares one OpenAI organisation, and the gateway prepends the same identity line to `instructions`. So all cloud chats open identically and land on the same cache machines.
  - **Follow-up:** add `prompt_cache_key` to `ALLOWED_FIELDS['responses']` in tsd-enterprise and deploy it. Then drop `&& !profile.account_sign_in` in `ResponsesCodec::build`.
  - **Order matters:** the app change must not ship before the gateway one.
  - Whether the deployed gateway matches `master` is **unverified**. The plan says it went live 2026-10-25 as obi.4048.
- **Anthropic format.** `messages` are forwarded as sent, `cache_control` included, and the gateway's identity text goes in a block of its own before the client's `system` block. Only `metadata` is dropped.
- **For R2/R6.**
  - In-array `role: "system"` messages and `developer` items pass through untouched, because the gateway does not inspect `messages` or `input`.
  - The gateway sends upstream only its backend's configured headers (`_headers()` in `upstream.py`), never the client's.
  - So R2's `clear_at` beta header (`anthropic-beta: mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`) reaches Anthropic only if it is added to the alias backend's `headers` in `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES`. Without it, `clear_at` is rejected as an unknown field.

## 2. A stable tool list

**Before.**

- `offered_tools` in `ProviderAgent.cpp` offered `object_import` only when the request's message had an importable model attachment. The turn that attached a model therefore sent a different tool list from the turn before and the turn after. On Anthropic that means a cold cache for the whole chat, twice.
- A call to `object_import` on any other turn was refused as `unknown_tool` before it ran.
- A call whose attachment could not be resolved failed with `not_found`: "The attached model is no longer available".

**Now.**

- **Registry.** `object_import` has `ToolAvailability::Always`. `ImportableAttachment` is removed from the enum.
- **Execution.** In `ToolExecutionCoordinator::execute`, an `attachmentId` that resolves to no stored model file fails with `invalid_arguments`, with the message: `No model file attached in this chat has the id "<id>". ## 3. The Anthropic cache breakpoint and skill text

**Where the breakpoints are today** (`AnthropicCodec.cpp`, all `{"type":"ephemeral"}`):

1. The last tool (`tools_json`, line 87).
2. The single `system` block (`build`, line 272).
3. The last block of the newest `user` message after role normalisation (`build`, line 262). It moves forward on every request.

A fired skill is sent as an in-array `role: "system"` message right after the user content or the tool results that fired it (`push_skills`). Its picture is a user image block, which merges into that user message, so the picture sits before breakpoint 3 and is cached. The skill text sits after it.

- On the request that fires it, the skill text is billed uncached at 1x.
- On the next request of the turn it is written to the cache at 1.25x.

That is M1's leak.

**Bytes after the last breakpoint, 26 recorded bodies.**

- **Method.** Each body was mapped to the Anthropic codec's message layout: developer items become system messages, then the codec's merge and normalisation rules apply. Then I counted the compact JSON after the breakpoint block.
- **Script.** `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin--claude-worktrees-cache-r8-f275c7/c449884d-06ef-4be3-ae77-8382bf117ba4/scratchpad/r8/after_breakpoint.py`, run as `python3 -I <script> tests/project_prompt/requests.json`.
- **Scope.** The system prompt and tools, about 41 KB, come before breakpoints 1 and 2 and are not counted.

| case | after the last breakpoint today (bytes) | of which skill text |
|---|---|---|
| model-imported-by-tool, model-opened-by-tool, model-opened-unnamed | 8,520 each | 8,446 (file-loaded) |
| advice-infill, answer-from-context, direct-change, issue-explain, issue-fix, loaded-vs-configured, reply-in-german, slice-warnings-ready, troubleshoot-first-layer | 5,309 each | 5,210 (print issues) |
| slice-refused-by-tool, slice-refused-then-ready | 3,640 each | 3,577 (slice failed) |
| after-intent | 1,329 | 1,288 (setup changed) |
| the other 11 cases | 0 | 0 |

- 15 of 26 bodies have bytes after the breakpoint, totalling 81,950. In every case it is one trailing system message holding the skill.
- With a breakpoint on the skill it would be 0 in every case.

**Why I did not move the breakpoint.** Source: Anthropic's mid-conversation system messages page (`platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages`), read 2026-10-29.

- **Under R2 it is an error.** R2 sends skills as turn-scoped messages (`clear_at: "next_user_message"`). The page says such a message carries "no `cache_control`" ("A cleared message is never part of a cache key, so a breakpoint on it could never match"). The API answers `cache_control is not permitted on a turn-scoped system message` with a 400. It says to "Put the breakpoint on the last block of the preceding user turn instead". Its agent-loop example puts it on the last `tool_result`. That is exactly today's breakpoint 3.
- **Today it is undocumented.** For a plain (`clear_at: "never"`) system message, the page says it "is itself cacheable", and that on the next turn "you can move your cache breakpoint past it". It never says `cache_control` is allowed on its blocks. Verifying that would need a live call, so I made none.

The rule was to change the placement only if it is right under both today's behaviour and R2's. Moving the breakpoint onto the skill is right under neither for certain, and is a 400 under R2. The code is unchanged.

**Recommendation for R2.**

1. **Keep breakpoint 3 where it is**, on the last block of the newest user message, which is the user turn before any skill. Never put `cache_control` on a turn-scoped message.
2. **The leak goes away under R2 without a breakpoint change.** The page says a turn-scoped message "renders only while no `role: "user"` message comes after it" and "A user message that carries only `tool_result` blocks counts". A cleared message "costs no input tokens".
   - So under R2 a skill's text is billed once, on the request that fires it, and is never written to the cache.
   - Today the same text is billed at 1x, then written at 1.25x, then read on the turn's later requests.
   - The 81,950 bytes above stay after the breakpoint on the firing request, but stop being written to the cache one request late.
3. **The clearing request reads the right entry.** The page says that on the request that clears a message, "the reusable cached prefix ends at the user turn before it, so only the one assistant turn between that message and the new user message is reprocessed". The entry it reads is the one breakpoint 3 wrote on the firing request. That is another reason not to move breakpoint 3.
4. **A design point R2 must settle (behaviour, not cost).** Because a `tool_result` message clears a turn-scoped message, the model sees the skill only on the request that fired it, not "for the rest of the turn".
   - That matches what the Responses codec does today, since it drops the skill from the next request.
   - It does not match today's Anthropic codec, which keeps the skill visible for the rest of the turn.
   - If the plan's "cleared at the next user message" meant the next message from the person, `clear_at` does not do that.
5. **A message after a tool result on smaller models.** The plan already notes that Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 may ignore a system message placed right after a tool result. Under R2 that is the only place a skill fired by a result can go.

**TTL (decision D7).** Confirmed: the codec sends no `ttl`. `ephemeral()` is `{"type":"ephemeral"}` at all three breakpoints, so the 5-minute default applies. Nothing in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/` mentions `ttl` or `1h`. The gateway forwards `cache_control` unchanged.

# Request-body logging (L0): report

Untracked working note, 2026-10-29. Branch `claude/cache-request-log-eca52c`, commit `282342b918`, on top of `claude/chat-history-cache` (`cd4162fa97`). Not pushed or merged.

## Problem

The chat-history cache work has to check that each model request opens with the bytes of the one before it. No full request body was kept anywhere. The prompt-test recorder's `requests.json` holds bodies for its own suite, with stored results cut at 4,000 characters, and the live harness modes printed only token counts.

## What I built

- **`tests/jusprin_support/RequestLog.hpp`** (header-only, so the harness and `agent_bridge_tests` share it with no CMake change). `RequestLog::transport(provider, inner)` wraps any `IAgentHttpTransport`; `RequestLog::agent(inner)` wraps any `IAgentService`, so the log knows each request's purpose (reply or title), request id and attempt. For the n-th request of a run it writes:
  - `NNNN-request.json`: the body exactly as the transport was given it, written before it is forwarded.
  - `NNNN-request.meta.json`: provider, URL, headers (`Authorization`, `x-api-key` and other credential headers redacted; `Idempotency-Key` kept), project id and chat id (chat ids restart in each project), purpose, request id, attempt, post time, body length.
  - `NNNN-response.sse`: the response stream as received.
  - `NNNN-response.json`: outcome (complete, error, cancelled, replaced, not_started), HTTP status, usage with the provider's own field names (Anthropic `cache_read_input_tokens`/`cache_creation_input_tokens` come through as-is), stop reason, assembled text, error. It reads both the Messages and the Responses stream.
- **Shell harness flag `--request-log <dir>`**, for `--live-agent`, `--manual-live-agent` and `--project-prompt-requests`. It refuses a non-empty directory and any other mode (exit 2). Documented in the header comment of `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` (where all flags are documented; there is no `tests/shell/README.md`) and in a new section of `tests/project_prompt/README.md`.
- **`tests/project_prompt/prefix_check.py LOG_DIR [--ignore-key KEY] [--json]`**. For consecutive requests of the same project, chat and purpose it reports the common byte prefix, the first differing byte, the JSON path of that byte in each body, and the path of the last differing byte. `[append]` means the later body is the earlier one with items added at the end of one array and every other byte unchanged. `--ignore-key cache_control` drops Anthropic's moving breakpoint (then the bodies are compared as Python re-serialises them, and the output says so). Unit tests: `tests/project_prompt/test_prefix_check.py`.

## How I verified it

- **Catch2** `[request-log]` in `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp` (appended at the end): two turns on the real host and provider loop, once per wire format, against the existing `RecordingProvider` fake. Each logged reply body equals the bytes the fake received; usage, stop reason, text, project and chat id, numbering and redaction are checked. I proved it can fail: making the logger append one byte to each body gave 4 byte-equality failures and 8 length failures; restored, it passes (150 assertions).
- **Whole agent suite**: 471 test cases, 16,575 assertions, all passed (Release build in this worktree).
- **`test_prefix_check.py`**: 9 tests pass. The "an append followed by a later change is not an append" test fails when the tail condition is removed.
- **Scripted harness run**: `--project-prompt-requests` on the `direct` conversation of `script.json` (two passes, scripted model, nothing sent over the network) with `--request-log` wrote 333 requests (1,332 files, largest body 1.4 MB). `prefix_check.py` reported all 329 pairs as `[append]` and took 7 seconds. The recorder's own output file was byte-identical with and without `--request-log`. `requests.json` and the baselines are untouched.

## What I could not verify, and things to know

- **No live run.** No model was called. The Anthropic path is tested only through the Catch2 fake; the Responses path through the fake and the scripted harness run. Real streams (OpenAI's `response.completed` usage, Anthropic's `message_start`/`message_delta` usage) follow the documented shapes the codecs already parse, but no real stream has gone through this logger yet.
- **The live harness mode only builds an OpenAI agent** on this branch. The Anthropic journey mode (`--plan-journey`) is uncommitted in `.claude/worktrees/opus-cost-batch`; to log it, wrap its `make_openai_http_transport()` with `log.transport("anthropic", …)` and its agent with `log.agent(…)`, the same way `install_harness_agent` does.
- **Not logged**: the printer panel's Agent and any agent the host rebuilds through its chat model source (a chat that picks a model other than the one the harness installed). Both are built from the app configuration through `make_openai_http_transport()` in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Covering them needs a small seam in production code (for example a test-settable transport wrapper used by `make_openai_http_transport`); I did not add one.
- **Reading the byte count on OpenAI**: the app writes JSON keys alphabetically, so a Responses body opens with `input` and has `instructions` and `tools` after it. The shared byte count of a clean append is then just the earlier `input`; read the kind and the last-difference path, not the count. This is about the JSON byte order only

- **Title requests.** They have no `chat_key`.

- `test_agent_bridge.cpp`, "every request of a chat carries one prompt_cache_key, and another chat another". It runs on the real host and loop. Chat A has a person turn with a slice call (two requests) and the app's turn after the slice. Chat B has one request. All three of chat A's requests carry `projectId/c-1`, and chat B's carries `projectId/c-2`.
- `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp`, "a request carries its chat's prompt_cache_key, except through JusPrin's gateway and for a title". It is a codec-level test covering:
  - OpenAI and OpenRouter get the key
  - the gateway does not
  - a title request does not

The `[history-prefix]` guard compares every non-prompt body field across requests. It stays unchanged, which confirms that the key does not vary within a chat.

**OpenRouter.** Its Responses API reference lists `prompt_cache_key` as an accepted optional string, but does not say what it does. Whether OpenRouter forwards it to OpenAI is **unverified**.

### Gateway finding (verified by reading the source)

The gateway source is on this machine: `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise`, branch `master` at `7ab63cc151`, the same as `origin/master`. See `web_ent/jusprin/v2/upstream.py`.

- **Unknown fields are refused, not forwarded.** `ALLOWED_FIELDS['responses']` is `model, store, stream, parallel_tool_calls, instructions, tools, input, reasoning`. `prepare()` answers any other top-level field with `400 invalid_request "Field "prompt_cache_key" is not allowed."`. Sending the key through the gateway would have failed every OpenAI-format JusPrin Cloud request. That is why the codec skips it for `account_sign_in`.
- **The gateway is where the key matters most.** Every JusPrin Cloud user shares one OpenAI organisation, and the gateway prepends the same identity line to `instructions`. So all cloud chats open identically and land on the same cache machines.
  - **Follow-up:** add `prompt_cache_key` to `ALLOWED_FIELDS['responses']` in tsd-enterprise and deploy it. Then drop `&& !profile.account_sign_in` in `ResponsesCodec::build`.
  - **Order matters:** the app change must not ship before the gateway one.
  - Whether the deployed gateway matches `master` is **unverified**. The plan says it went live 2026-10-25 as obi.4048.
- **Anthropic format.** `messages` are forwarded as sent, `cache_control` included, and the gateway's identity text goes in a block of its own before the client's `system` block. Only `metadata` is dropped.
- **For R2/R6.**
  - In-array `role: "system"` messages and `developer` items pass through untouched, because the gateway does not inspect `messages` or `input`.
  - The gateway sends upstream only its backend's configured headers (`_headers()` in `upstream.py`), never the client's.
  - So R2's `clear_at` beta header (`anthropic-beta: mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`) reaches Anthropic only if it is added to the alias backend's `headers` in `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES`. Without it, `clear_at` is rejected as an unknown field.

## 2. A stable tool list

**Before.**

- `offered_tools` in `ProviderAgent.cpp` offered `object_import` only when the request's message had an importable model attachment. The turn that attached a model therefore sent a different tool list from the turn before and the turn after. On Anthropic that means a cold cache for the whole chat, twice.
- A call to `object_import` on any other turn was refused as `unknown_tool` before it ran.
- A call whose attachment could not be resolved failed with `not_found`: "The attached model is no longer available".

**Now.**

- **Registry.** `object_import` has `ToolAvailability::Always`. `ImportableAttachment` is removed from the enum.
- **Execution.** In `ToolExecutionCoordinator::execute`, an `attachmentId` that resolves to no stored model file fails with `invalid_arguments`, with the message: `No model file attached in this chat has the id "<id>". Nothing was imported. Use an attachment id from the person's message; if they attached no model file, ask them to attach it.`
- **Why `invalid_arguments`.**
  - It keeps the call in the "fix the call" group of `ToolErrors.hpp`, where `unknown_tool` already put it.
  - `not_found` means "read the state again, then call again", and re-reading the workspace cannot find an attachment.
  - The "Ask the person" codes (`opened_before`, `workspace_unavailable`) mean other conditions.
  - The message names the step.
- **Side effect.** A model attached in an earlier message of the chat can now be imported later, because the resolver looks the id up in the whole document.

**Tests.**

- `test_agent_bridge.cpp`, "the tool list is the same on every request of a chat, whatever a message attaches". It runs on the real host with the Anthropic wire format:
  - turn 1 has no attachment
  - turn 2 attaches a model and imports it, adding one object
  - turn 3 calls `object_import` with an id that names nothing
  - all 5 requests carry byte-identical `tools`, `object_import` included
  - the turn-3 call comes back as an `is_error` result with `invalid_arguments` and the message, and adds no object
- **Proved fail-first.** I temporarily put back the old rule (offer `object_import` only with an importable attachment), rebuilt and ran the test. It failed 5 of 28 assertions: the attachment turn's two requests carried a different tool list, and the turn-3 call got `unknown_tool`. I then restored the source.
- `test_tool_coordinator.cpp`: the unresolvable-attachment case now expects `invalid_arguments` and the exact message.
- `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp`: the tool list with a model attachment equals the list without one.
- Updated counts: from 29 to 30 tools in three tests.

**Knock-on changes outside the Agent sources.** Both are generated or test files, and both follow directly from the change:

- **`tests/project_prompt/project_tools.json`.**
  - Regenerated with `JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PROJECT_TOOLS=1`: 31 tools, 39,661 bytes compact, up from 38,792 (+869).
  - The README and a comment in `run_prompt_tests.py` were updated to match.
- **`tests/shell/project_prompt_scenario.inc`.**
  - The prompt recorder used to strip `object_import` before comparing a request's tools with `project_tools.json`. It now compares directly.
  - It also leaves `prompt_cache_key` out of recorded bodies; that is commit `c5bd57c8eb`.
  - The file compiles: the object file was built on its own.
  - The harness was **not run**, because that needs a full app build, which I did not start on the shared machine.
  - The shell-harness session (L0, `cache-log`) should know about this change.

**Behaviour change, not evaluated.** Every project-chat request now describes `object_import`, about 870 bytes, including turns with nothing attached. Per the plan's rule, steps that change what the model reads run the prompt evals. **No live evals were run.** That needs Kenneth's approval of a batch.

**Not changed.** `skill_read` is still offered only when the page lists skills. That list is fixed for a host session, and the printer sessions name their own tools, so it does not vary within a chat.

## 3. The Anthropic cache breakpoint and skill text

**Where the breakpoints are today** (`AnthropicCodec.cpp`, all `{"type":"ephemeral"}`):

1. The last tool (`tools_json`, line 87).
2. The single `system` block (`build`, line 272).
3. The last block of the newest `user` message after role normalisation (`build`, line 262). It moves forward on every request.

A fired skill is sent as an in-array `role: "system"` message right after the user content or the tool results that fired it (`push_skills`). Its picture is a user image block, which merges into that user message, so the picture sits before breakpoint 3 and is cached. The skill text sits after it.

- On the request that fires it, the skill text is billed uncached at 1x.
- On the next request of the turn it is written to the cache at 1.25x.

That is M1's leak.

**Bytes after the last breakpoint, 26 recorded bodies.**

- **Method.** Each body was mapped to the Anthropic codec's message layout: developer items become system messages, then the codec's merge and normalisation rules apply. Then I counted the compact JSON after the breakpoint block.
- **Script.** `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin--claude-worktrees-cache-r8-f275c7/c449884d-06ef-4be3-ae77-8382bf117ba4/scratchpad/r8/after_breakpoint.py`, run as `python3 -I <script> tests/project_prompt/requests.json`.
- **Scope.** The system prompt and tools, about 41 KB, come before breakpoints 1 and 2 and are not counted.

| case | after the last breakpoint today (bytes) | of which skill text |
|---|---|---|
| model-imported-by-tool, model-opened-by-tool, model-opened-unnamed | 8,520 each | 8,446 (file-loaded) |
| advice-infill, answer-from-context, direct-change, issue-explain, issue-fix, loaded-vs-configured, reply-in-german, slice-warnings-ready, troubleshoot-first-layer | 5,309 each | 5,210 (print issues) |
| slice-refused-by-tool, slice-refused-then-ready | 3,640 each | 3,577 (slice failed) |
| after-intent | 1,329 | 1,288 (setup changed) |
| the other 11 cases | 0 | 0 |

- 15 of 26 bodies have bytes after the breakpoint, totalling 81,950. In every case it is one trailing system message holding the skill.
- With a breakpoint on the skill it would be 0 in every case.
